info.title: EVS Cerebrum RCP
info.description:
Note this is an initial beta release of the protocol and subject to change - All device values which can be obtained using HTTP GET commands can also be optionally received via the websocket back-channel, using the subscribe and unsubscribe URIs. - On subscribing to a URI, it's initial value will delivered. As such it is not envisaged that there should be a need to both GET and subscribe to a specific object. - When connecting the websocket, the token obtained during login will need to be provided (details to follow) - If the websocket is closed, all associated subscriptions will be dropped - All packets sent over the websocket will have the same structure as the related get response, but with a wrapper around them to give the context of the data - In order to improve throughput the /batch endpoint can be used. I haven't got a good schema for this yet so see https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/batch-requests for an idea of where this is going - The longer term intention will be to support HTTP2 and multiplexing, but batching may still be useful to allow multiple operations to arrive at the service concurrently - We will try to avoid creating 'combined' request type endpoints (set many objects at once) - batching should be used for this if needed. The assumption is the overhead of the batching should be minimal on modern HW. Routing is likely to be an exception where cross level takes are very common - In Version 2, subscription are created using the Backchannel rather than via the REST API
Addressable device endpoints use several standard URL parameters to uniquely specify the targeted device: - {deviceName} is the name (or IP address) given to the root device in Cerebrum's System View. - {deviceIndex} relates to subdevices - if the targeted device is a single generic device, this is 0. If it is a subdevice, it is the index of the subdevice. - {instanceName} is used when the operation target is a member of a generic device which manages multiple devices at once. The GenericDevice object tree for these devices will expose the multiple managed devices as a table. This, for example, allows targeting a single camera through a single GenericDevice which manages a chain of cameras. In this case, it should be set to the index of the target within the object tree's table. In all other cases it should be set to '1'.
The following generic devices are currently supported: - Switchers - Panasonic Kairos - Audio Mixers - Lawo A__UHD Core - Graphics - Erizos - Cameras - Panasonic Cameras - Multiviewers - EVS Neuron View

routeMasterSourceDeviceUpdate.description:
The device binding to apply to this source on this level - the "Device", "Device Level" and "Source" columns of the router configuration. At least one field must be supplied and only the supplied fields are modified.

"name", "typeId" and "deviceLevel" may only be supplied on a level whose "multipleDevices" is true; on every other level the device is fixed by the level itself and supplying them returns a 400. Read multipleDevices from the level to find out which applies.

A conventional device IO and an IP sender are mutually exclusive. Supplying "io" clears "senderReceiver", and supplying "senderReceiver" clears "io" and is rejected with a 400 when the bound device is not an IP router. Supplying "deviceLevel" greater than 0 also clears "senderReceiver".

Clearing "name" clears "deviceLevel" with it, and setting "ignore" clears both "io" and "senderReceiver".

name.description:
The name of the device to bind this level to. An empty string clears the device, and with it the
device level. Only valid when the level allows multiple devices.

typeId.description:
The device type id qualifying "name", as returned by the GET. Supply it whenever "name" is supplied.
Only valid when the level allows multiple devices.

deviceLevel.description:
The level on the device, which is not the RouteMaster level id. 0 clears it.
Only valid when the level allows multiple devices.

io.description: The input number on the device, counted from 1. 0 clears the binding.

senderReceiver.description:
The uid of the IP sender to bind this level to. An empty string clears it.
Only valid when the bound device is an IP router.

subChannel.description:
The sub channel within the bound IO or sender. In the router configuration this is chosen as part of the
"Source" selection rather than as a column of its own, and it is only applied when this level has a
device IO or a sender bound.

inhibit.description:
Inhibit this source on this level only. In the router configuration this is chosen as the "Inhibit" entry
of the "Source" selection rather than as a column of its own. It is separate both from the IO wide
tieLineInhibit and from the level's inhibited source list.

ignore.description:
Ignore this level's binding and use the level default source instead. In the router configuration this is
chosen as the "Ignore" entry of the "Source" selection. Setting it clears the device IO and sender.

routeMasterSourceLevelUpdate.description:
The configuration of one RouteMaster source on one level. At least one field must be supplied and only the
supplied fields are modified.

tags.description:
The tags to set on this source for this level, replacing any tags already set. An empty array clears the tags without inheriting the level default, which leaves the source explicitly untagged on this level.

Tags are stored pipe separated, so a tag may not itself contain a pipe. The router configuration shows them joined into one comma separated cell, but they are distinct tags and are matched individually.

tagsInherit.description:
Set to true to drop any tags set directly on this source on this level so that it inherits the level
default instead. Supply either this or "tags", not both.

clear.description:
Set to true to remove this level's configuration entirely, clearing the device binding, sub channel,
tags and flags in one go. When true no other field may be supplied.

routeMasterSourceCreate.description:
The configuration of the RouteMaster sources to create. The body describes the first source and takes the same fields as a source update, so a fully configured source can be created in one request.

When "count" is greater than 1 the remaining sources are derived from the first by incrementing: the last group of digits in "mnemonic" and in each alternate mnemonic is stepped by one per source, preserving any zero padding ("SRC-0001" becomes "SRC-0002"), and each level's device "io" is stepped by one. A level bound to an IP sender instead takes the next sender in that router's list. Every other field, including the device name, device level, sub channel, tags and the tie line inhibit, is copied unchanged to all of them.

"virtual" excludes the rest of the body: a virtual source has no device binding, so supplying any other field alongside "virtual": true is rejected with a 400. "clear" is not valid on a level here either, since there is nothing yet to clear.

count.description: The number of sources to create

virtual.description:
Create the sources as virtual rather than backed by a physical device IO. Mutually exclusive with every
other field in this body.

mnemonic.description: The original mnemonic of the first source. Optional.

tieLineInhibit.description: Inhibit these sources from being used as part of a tie line. Optional.

federationUid.description:
Link the created sources to federation sources instead of configuring them locally, by giving the id of the federation source the first one is linked to. Optional.

A linked source takes its mnemonic, levels, tags and tie line settings from the federation source, so those fields are redundant here and are ignored. "alternateMnemonics" is the exception: it stays local and is applied on top of the link, so a linked source can still carry its own operator, city, matches and tech mnemonics. "virtual" also still applies.

When "count" is greater than 1 each subsequent source is linked to the next federation source, taken in mnemonic order as the router configuration does, not by adding one to this id.

levels.description:
The per level configuration of the first source, indexed by level_<id>. Optional; a level the source
does not exist on returns a 400.

routerIOTagList.description:

with duplicates collapsed.

An empty array means the IO carries no tags on any level.

A linked source takes its mnemonic, levels, tags and tie line settings from the federation source. "alternateMnemonics" stays local and overrides the federation source's, so it is still the source's own.

tieLineInhibit.description: Inhibit this source from being used as part of a tie line. Optional.

routeMasterFederationDestinationCreate.description:
The configuration of the federation RouteMaster destinations to create. The body describes the first destination and takes the same fields as a federation destination update.

tags.description:
Control and status of routing (e.g. video, audio and data).

These endpoints implement filtering via query strings which look like <FieldName>(<operator>)=<Value>. For example "DestinationId(in)=1,4..5,17". Including "X..Y" allows you to filter including any values between X and Y

You can omit the operator if you just want to include a single value - e.g. "DestinationId=1".

Each filterable field will support different operators and these will be documented on the specific endpoint. Multiple filter parameters can be specified, e.g. "DestinationId(in)=1,4-5,17&DestLevelId=3".

Subscriptions also support these filter query strings, so you can receive updates on just the levels or destinations you are interested in.

tags.name: routemaster
tags.description:
Configuration of the RouteMaster sources, destinations and levels, in both local and federated systems.

Local and federation IOs are separate collections - /routemaster/sources, /routemaster/destinations, /routemaster/federation-sources and /routemaster/federation-destinations - each with its own ids, so the same id can exist in two of them and refer to two different IOs.

A GET on a collection returns its ids as an array of strings, each of which can be appended to the path to address that IO and obtain its full configuration. These endpoints take no query parameters.

A federation IO's id is the uuid the federation assigns it and cannot be set or changed. A local IO instead carries "federationUid", which links it to a federation IO; a linked IO takes its mnemonic, levels, tags and tie line settings from the federation IO, while its alternate mnemonics stay local and override the federation ones.

Tags and the tie line inhibit apply to federation IOs exactly as they do to local ones, and are replicated to the federation.

An IO is configured per level. Each level carries the device binding - the device, the level on that device and the input/output or IP sender/receiver - along with that level's tags and inhibit flags. A conventional device IO and an IP sender/receiver are mutually exclusive on a level. Read them from the "levels" map of a single IO and write them through the "levels" map of a PATCH.

Tags are free form strings held per IO per level, and are used to match compatible sources and destinations when a route is requested by tag. An IO may carry several tags on a level; the router configuration shows them joined into one comma separated cell, but they are distinct tags and are matched individually. A level carries a default set of source tags and destination tags which an IO inherits until it defines tags of its own; "tagsInherited" tells you which of the two you are looking at. Clearing an IO's tags with an empty array leaves it explicitly untagged, while "tagsInherit" returns it to the level default.

Creating and modifying levels is not supported through this API.

get.summary: Obtains the ids of the configured local RouteMaster sources
get.description:
Obtains the ids of every configured local RouteMaster source. Each entry can be appended to this path to
address an individual source, which is where its configuration is obtained from.

post.description:
Appends "count" new local sources, configured from the supplied body. The body describes the first source; any further sources are derived from it by incrementing the mnemonics and each level's device IO, so a contiguous block of wired sources can be created in one request.

The ids of the created sources are allocated by Cerebrum; re-query the id list to obtain them.

get.summary: Obtains a single local RouteMaster source
get.description:

device bound to each of them and the tags in effect.

patch.summary: Update a local RouteMaster source

Only the supplied fields are modified.

get.summary: Obtains the uuids of the configured federation RouteMaster sources
get.description:
Obtains the uuids of every configured federation RouteMaster source. Each entry can be appended to this path to address an individual federation source, which is where its configuration is obtained from.

Federation and local sources are held separately and each have their own ids, so the same id can exist in both and refer to two different sources.

post.description:
Appends "count" new federation sources, configured from the supplied body. The body describes the first source; any further sources are derived from it by incrementing the mnemonics and each level's device IO.

The uuids of the created sources are allocated by the federation; re-query the id list to obtain them.

patch.summary: Update a federation RouteMaster source

A federation source's uuid is assigned by the federation and cannot be changed here.

post.description:

The uuids of the created destinations are allocated by the federation; re-query the id list to obtain them.

get.description:
Allows the querying of a single VALUE or TABLE node.

 If a VALUE node is queried, the current value and metadata of the object will be returned.

 If a TABLE node is queried, the indices of the table will be returned.

 If a non-VALUE non-TABLE node is queried, an empty object will be returned.

indices.description: Returned if a table node is queried, and contains the indices of the table. Not returned if a non-table node is queried.

object.description: Returned if a VALUE node is queried, and contains the value and metadata of the object. Not returned if a non-VALUE node is queried.

current.example: Current value of the object. Type depends on the object (string, bool or number).

writable.description: Whether the object is writable or not.

allowedValues.description: If the object is an enum, this will contain the allowed values. Otherwise it will not be returned.
